current_example.problem: What is the solution to the equation $6^x - 6^5= 0?$
current_example.worked_solution:
First, we isolate the term with the variable exponent by adding $6^5$ to both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}{6}^{x}-{6}^{5} & =0 \\ {6}^{x}-{6}^{5}+{6}^{5} & =0+{6}^{5} \\ {6}^{x}-\cancel{{6}^{5}}+\cancel{{6}^{5}} & =0+{6}^{5} \\ {6}^{x} & ={6}^{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Since both sides of the equation share the same base $(6),$ we can equate the exponents. 

$$
\begin{aligned}{6}^{x} & ={6}^{5} \\ x & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is ${\color{blue}x} = {\color{blue}5}.$
